sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Brian Burns
articles.description: A year after pulling its music in protest, the duo is back on Spotify. For Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn, that journey has been frustrating, eye-opening — and full of smaller victories.
articles.title: 'They touch everything': Sylvan Esso confronts the Spotify dilemma, again

articles.author: Bill Chappell
articles.description: The fall equinox, which arrives Tuesday in the U.S., brings shorter days, and chances to witness alignment between Earth and the sun. It's a modern version of ancient observances of a celestial shift.
articles.title: What the equinox 'henge' effect tells us about U.S. cities

articles.author: Terry Gross
articles.description: A self-described "folkie to the bone," Giddens sings and plays banjo and fiddle in this interview. Her latest album, Hope Is the Thing with Feathers, takes its name from an Emily Dickinson poem.
articles.title: Rhiannon Giddens' banjo connects her to her ancestors: 'The spirits come through'

articles.author: Joel Rose
articles.description: The Federal Aviation Administration launched an ambitious $875-million-dollar push to make the U.S. airspace more efficient. But critics say it won't solve bigger problems with air traffic control.
articles.title: Aviation regulators turn to AI to help manage the nation's airspace

articles.author: David Folkenflik
articles.description: Paramount's owners have made concessions to 12 Democratic state attorneys general to settle a lawsuit that endangered the media company's bid for its larger Hollywood rival, Warner Bros. Discovery.
articles.title: Paramount makes concessions to salvage $111 billion Warner Bros. Discovery deal

articles.author: Sam Gringlas
articles.description: While many Republican candidates, even in some critical tossup races, still back President Trump's baseless claims about election integrity, some GOP voters say they are ready to move on.
articles.title: Many GOP candidates still echo Trump's 2020 claims. Lots of voters want to move on

articles.author: Rachel Cramer
articles.description: The U.S. gets nearly a third of its pork from Iowa. One family is making the switch from pigs to more sustainable specialty mushrooms and trying to show other pig farmers how they did it.
articles.title: This farm raised thousands of pigs for slaughter. Now it's growing mushrooms instead

articles.author: Esme Nicholson
articles.description: German Chancellor Freidrich Merz conceded that the night spells "disaster" for the political center, but assured the public he'd push ahead with his federal agenda of tax and welfare reforms.
articles.title: Germany's leader stands his ground after his party loses in state elections

articles.author: Michele Kelemen
articles.description: United Nations head António Guterres returns to New York for his final U.N. General Assembly as diplomacy falters over wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, and the global body faces deep divisions.
articles.title: What to know as world leaders converge at the United Nations this week

articles.author: Scott Neuman
articles.description: With striking speed, the widespread debate around data centers has become a fault line in American communities, cutting across political parties and forging unexpected alliances.
articles.title: The data center backlash is reshaping American politics — one community at a time

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Jim Chalmers was also asked earlier if the government would support a national royal commission into violence against women and children. He said the government had chosen to increase resourcing for child and family violence and domestic violence, adding to the ABC:
We’re trying to deal with the sources of all of this violence, whether it be more security in the housing system, whether it be the monetised misogyny that we see online – there are a whole range of factors feeding in here.
We do acknowledge that all of this violence is obviously entirely unacceptable. It’s horrific in every way. That’s why we’ve increased the resources and that’s why we all need to do better to do everything we can to make a difference here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: police investigating possible organised crime links after 11-year-old boy shot in Sydney apartment

articles.author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
articles.description:
One academic says prediction for 2066 ‘is negligent in ignoring the economic damage’ on the horizon 

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian government snapshot of life in 40 years has been sharply criticised for underplaying the economic and social damage expected due to the worsening climate crisis.
The government’s seventh intergenerational report, which projects out to 2066, finds the effects of global heating four decades from now are “highly uncertain”, pointing to the pace of the global energy transition as a key source of unpredictability.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Intergenerational report underplays effect of climate crisis on Australia’s future, experts say

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Trump’s announcement on Russia ally comes as he steps up his trade war with Canada, a long-term US ally and top supplier of potash
President Donald Trump has said he is working on a “massive” deal to buy fertiliser from Belarus, pivoting away from main supplier Canada amid an escalating trade dispute, and moving instead toward an ally of Russia.
“The United States is working on a massive deal with respect to the purchase of Potash from Belarus,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “The pricing would be for substantially less than we are currently paying to Canada, very good news for our farmers and ranchers.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump seeks ‘massive’ Belarus fertiliser deal amid Canada trade war

articles.author: Amelia Hill
articles.description:
Women escaping abusive partners abroad could get new protections from legal analysis of Hague convention
British mothers who bring their children with them when returning to the UK after fleeing from domestic abuse abroad – which can lead to them being accused of abduction – could be given greater legal protection and support.
The government has agreed to examine how domestic abuse features in international child abduction cases, with a view to giving survivors of domestic abuse more help fighting partners’ demands that they return children to their home countries.
In the UK, call the national domestic abuse helpline on 0808 2000 247, or visit Women’s Aid. In the US, the domestic violence hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). In Australia, the national family violence counselling service is on 1800 737 732. Other international helplines may be found via www.befrienders.org.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hope for UK mothers accused of child abduction after fleeing domestic violence

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Police don’t know if shooting was accidental as Labor attacks opposition vow to scrap gun buyback announced after Bondi massacre

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The shooting of an 11-year-old boy in Sydney’s north-west was a “tragic reminder” of the danger of guns, the New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, has said while the opposition defends “backflipping” on a gun buyback.
The child was transported to Westmead Children’s hospital in a critical condition on Monday evening after suffering gunshot wounds to his face and neck at a unit in Norwest, NSW police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Political fight over gun buyback after boy, 11, shot in the face and neck in Sydney apartment

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos, Chris Hippensteel, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

The three news outlets President Trump banned from the White House last Friday have filed their anticipated lawsuit against his administration to restore their access.
In the new complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on Monday, CNN, MS Now and Politico alleged that Trump had violated the First Amendment and due process by stripping the outlets of their White House access in a blatant act of retaliation for coverage he disliked.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he’ll probably lose lawsuit brought by news outlets he banned from White House, blaming judge appointed by ‘TRUMP’ – as it happened

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to fatally shooting Jesse Baird, 26, and his partner, 29-year-old Luke Davies, with police service weapon in 2024

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast


A former police officer claims he killed two men in self-defence and began cleaning up the crime scene because he “panicked”, a Sydney court has heard.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting 26-year-old Jesse Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, 29, with a police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former cop Beau Lamarre-Condon argues self-defence in double murder trial citing struggle over gun

articles.author: Ariana Baio in New York and Maanvi Singh
articles.description:
White House promoted its own ‘Trump TV’ feed online after ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC decline to participate
The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump after the administration banned journalists from several outlets from entering the White House grounds.
The collective decision came after the barred outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – sued the administration on Monday, saying the president’s actions were a violation of their first amendment rights.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

articles.author: José Olivares in New York and David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Republican president said he hoped the democratic socialist would be a ‘great mayor’ for New York City
Donald Trump said on Monday that he hoped Zohran Mamdani would be a “great mayor” for New York, an unusually warm assessment of the democratic socialist leader whom the president and his Republican allies have spent months holding up as a symbol of the Democratic party’s alleged embrace of “communism” ahead of the November midterms.
At a news conference following their closed-door meeting at Gracie Mansion, Trump and Mamdani appeared friendly as they have in previous meetings. Mamdani said he and Trump held a “wide-ranging” discussion, which touched on affordable housing and immigration, but did not offer extensive details regarding any disagreements between them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump and Mamdani appear friendly after ‘wide-ranging’ meeting at Gracie Mansion

articles.author: Sara Sneath in New York and Adam Morton
articles.description:
Prime minister says ‘climate security is the new national security’ in keynote speech in New York

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Australia understands the dangers of global heating and the urgency of climate action as much as any other country, Anthony Albanese has said in a keynote speech shortly before the United Nations general assembly.
Giving the opening address at a Climate Week event in New York on Monday, the prime minister said Australians had experienced the impact of climate breakdown up close with a series of disastrous bushfires and floods in the past decades.
Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Short on substance’: Albanese urges climate action on world stage – but advocates say Australia failing on fossil fuels

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Thousands of flights were delayed or canceled after a primary line failed and a backup fiber-optic cable was severed
Airport operations across the US north-east resumed Monday evening after a communications line failure snarled flights at some of the country’s busiest airports, leading to thousands of flight cancellations and delays.
Flights were halted at several airports after a primary communications line failed at a key Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) facility in Philadelphia. The backup fiber optic line, which delivers internet service, was inadvertently severed by a railroad construction crew, resulting in a telecommunications crash and hundreds of canceled flights at Newark, LaGuardia, JFK, Philadelphia and Boston airports.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flights resume across US north-east after FAA communications failure

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Environmental groups vow to continue opposition to deal that would expand site for Elon Musk rocket company
A federal judge on Monday refused to block the Trump administration from giving SpaceX more than 700 acres of wildlife refuge as part of a land swap in Texas, while environmental groups vowed to continue their legal challenge.
US district judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr declined the plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction to prevent the parcel exchange, saying they failed to prove it would worsen ecological risks to a Gulf coast region already transformed by billionaire Elon Musk’s rocket operations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US judge declines to block transfer of wildlife refuge land to Musk’s SpaceX

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Will Parman
articles.description:
Experts say trend across England probably reflects swifter access to diagnoses as wealthier families go private
Some of the most affluent areas of England have had the sharpest rises in the proportion of young people claiming disability benefits for ADHD and autism since the pandemic, according to new research.
Claims for the personal independence payment (Pip) benefit for these health conditions were typically proportionally far higher in deprived areas with higher rates of poverty, low educational outcomes and insecure employment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Young people’s Pip claims for ADHD and autism ‘rising fastest in affluent areas’

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Changes could save £33bn and result in average of four extra years of good health for people, report says
The NHS in England could prevent 20,000 deaths and save £33bn a year by cutting red tape and boosting productivity, a report says.
Research by the Health Foundation found the health service has been held back for decades by excessive regulation, short-term planning and insufficient capability to deliver major change.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut NHS red tape and boost productivity to prevent 20,000 early deaths a year in England, report urges

articles.author: Tobi Thomas health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Accra Reset’s report states countries in the region and global south should take greater control of their health development after USAID debacle
The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put has put healthcare in Africa and the Global South “under growing strain” a new report warns.
The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthcare in Africa ‘under growing strain’ after US withdrawal from aid programs, report warns

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Andy Burnham seeks stability in Middle East to bring down prices at home as first meeting with Trump looms
The UK has agreed to provide defensive air support to Saudi Arabia to help counter Houthi fighters and restore stability in the Middle East while driving down the cost of living at home, Andy Burnham has said, ahead of his first meeting with Donald Trump.
The prime minister said he had agreed to a request for air-to-air refuelling of Saudi jets to defend energy infrastructure against the Iran-backed rebels and help keep oil flowing from the Gulf to ease global economic turmoil.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to give support to Saudi jets in attempt to counter Houthi fighters

articles.author: Alexandra Topping and Peter Walker
articles.description:
At Lib Dems’ conference in Brighton, leader will accuse Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and ‘tech bros’ to solve problem
Ed Davey is to call for a global nuclear-style non-proliferation treaty to halt the development of super-intelligent AI when he makes his keynote speech at the Liberal Democrat conference, accusing Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and “tech bros” to solve the problem.
When he addresses the faithful on the final day of the gathering in Brighton, the party leader will call for a global pause on super-intelligent AI, comparing it to a nuclear arms race that could result in technology that could “destroy us all”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Halt super-intelligent AI with non-proliferation treaty, Ed Davey to say

articles.author: Jess Cartner-Morley
articles.description:
Textile designer brings florals, vines and smiley doodles to brand’s luxury checks for one-off paired collection
Burberry and Celia Birtwell are both national treasures of sorts. One is Britain’s grandest luxury name, the other the textile designer who dressed bohemian 1960s London in her prints and has a place in art history as David Hockney’s favourite muse.
Burberry’s designer, Daniel Lee, has always loved Birtwell’s prints. When the two met this spring, he fell for “her energy, and her zest for life”, and a one-off Burberry meets Birtwell collection that closed London fashion week was born.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Celia Birtwell ‘humanises’ Burberry in London fashion week closing show

articles.author: Alice Speri
articles.description:
Students faced prison terms and thousands of dollars in restitution over campus protest against Israel’s war on Gaza
Five Stanford University students who faced prison sentences and thousands of dollars in restitution in connection to a campus protest against Israel’s war on Gaza had all charges dropped on Monday.
The students also had their restitution severely reduced, ending a two-year legal saga that also saw the lead prosecutor in the case removed by the court.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Charges dropped against Stanford students over pro-Palestine protest

articles.author: Associated Press in Bogotá
articles.description:
Wildfire forces evacuations and burns through mountains surrounding Villa de Leyva in the north-east 
Colombian authorities declared a public calamity as a wildfire burned through mountains surrounding one of the country’s best-known colonial towns in the north-east, scorching large swaths of vegetation and forcing evacuations.
Nearly 20 active fires are burning across the South American country. Dry conditions have increased fire danger in Colombia as it braces for the effects of El Niño, which can help wildfires spread.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Colombia declares public calamity as wildfire threatens popular tourist area

articles.author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
articles.description:
US president reportedly changed his mind over Saudi Arabia’s pleas for assistance as bombs were being loaded
Houthi fighters are moving to seize strategic heights in Yemen that would cut the Red Sea coast off from areas held ​by Saudi-backed forces after Donald Trump called off US strikes on the group at the last minute, reportedly as bombs were being loaded on to aircraft.
Amid increasingly heavy fighting in Yemen, which has displaced tens of thousands of people in recent weeks, the New York Times reported on Monday that the US president had flip-flopped wildly in recent days after a call from Saudi Arabia for US strikes on the Houthis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthis move to seize strategic terrain after Trump calls off airstrikes at last minute

articles.author: Tiago Rogero, South America correspondent
articles.description:
Dozens of US attacks on boats in the Pacific and Caribbean have killed more than 230 people since September 2025
A special rapporteur for the UN human rights council has concluded that there are “reasonable grounds to believe” that the United States attacks on boats allegedly carrying drugs in the Pacific and Caribbean “constituted crimes against humanity”.
The boat strikes, carried out since September 2025 on the stated grounds of stopping drugs being trafficked by sea to the US, have killed more than 230 people. The latest, on Saturday, killed four people in the Caribbean.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US strikes on alleged drug boats may constitute ‘crimes against humanity’, UN expert says

articles.author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
articles.description:
Merz seeks to shore up support after CDU loses two state elections and is ejected from Mecklenburg parliament

Latest German election humiliation puts Merz on borrowed time as CDU unrest grows

Germany’s beleaguered leader, Friedrich Merz, has vowed to keep his fractious coalition government together for the good of the country’s “democratic future” after his conservative party suffered a drubbing at the polls in two state elections.
Merz, who has vowed to plough ahead with an unpopular reform agenda, dismissed speculation over his position, saying it was vital that he and his coalition government remained in place.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chancellor vows to stay on for Germany’s ‘democratic future’ after latest loss to far-right AfD

articles.author: Frances Mao (now) and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
CDU suffered heavy losses in two regional elections, including in home state of former leader Angela Merkel, where it polled just 4.9%
Staying in Germany, tens of thousands of automotive workers at Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and other car brands are protesting on factory floors across the country today for government and management help to save their jobs.

 Volkswagen has announced plans to cut 100,000 jobs in the next three years and BMW and Mercedes are also slashing their workforce.
The problem is a near-existential one: the rise of Chinese EV carmakers with their cheaper, and in some cases more advanced models, has thrown the German car industry into crisis. The Germans, who have been far slower to transition to electric vehicles, simply aren’t selling as many cars anymore and need to retool to keep up.

 The fears are reflective of wider concerns over Europe’s industrial base being eroded by Chinese competition. Union leaders – pointing to state support for Chinese car makers- are calling for government support, like energy subsidies and financial help, or putting up trade protections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Germany’s Merz ‘grateful’ centre-left SPD wants to stay in coalition after CDU’s heavy losses – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Officials say man was critically injured and officer was wounded in Yom Kippur incident near Belleville synagogue
A police officer and a man were wounded in an exchange of gunfire on Sunday near a synagogue in Ontario as members of the Jewish community marked Yom Kippur, authorities said. The man was hospitalized in life-threatening condition.
The Canadian province’s special investigations unit said the exchange of gunfire happened near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, about 110 miles (160km) east of Toronto. Belleville police said the officer encountered the man at about 7.10pm and that both were taken to a hospital.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man and police officer wounded in exchange of gunfire near Ontario synagogue

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Police crack down on family and political supporters of former PM who say authorities are ‘slowly killing’ him in prison
Three sisters of Pakistan’s incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan have been arrested amid a heavy-handed government crackdown on plans for a nationwide protest to demand Khan’s release.
The lawyer for the three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, said on Monday that they had all been detained and jailed for 30 days under a warrant that accused them of being a threat to public order.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan jails sisters of Imran Khan before protest seeking his release

articles.author: Luke Harding and agencies
articles.description:
United Russia party’s record victory in tightly controlled vote likely to be used as evidence of support for war against Ukraine
Russia’s new parliament will include 49 deputies who have taken part in the war against Ukraine, officials have said after a landslide victory by the ruling United Russia party in widely criticised elections.
The pro-Kremlin party won a record 355 seats in the country’s 450-seat Duma lower house of parliament, according to preliminary figures. The result further consolidates Vladimir Putin’s grip on power and gives United Russia a super-majority bigger than its previous 2016 record of 343 seats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Putin consolidates grip on Russia as 49 Ukraine war veterans elected to parliament

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests
Google has been fined more than €400m (£345m) over the way it processed users’ location data, following claims that the tech giant had manipulated users into agreeing to be constantly tracked on their mobile phones.
The fine, imposed by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC), comes after complaints from multiple European consumer organisations that Google was following every step users took.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Google fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location data

articles.author: Jodie Woodcock for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storm system expected to hit Izu Islands as it strengthens. Meanwhile, Atlantic hurricane season is unusually quiet
Tropical Storm Dujuan is skirting the coast of Japan and despite avoiding a direct landfall, is still expected to leave its mark. Dujuan briefly reached typhoon status on Friday before weakening to a tropical storm again on Sunday morning. But it is expected to restrengthen back to a typhoon by Tuesday morning. Sustained winds could reach 80mph (129km/h), with gusts approaching 100mph.
Although mainland Japan has avoided a direct hit, Dujuan’s track takes it across the Izu Islands, where evacuation warnings are in place. Heavy rain, flooding and landslide alerts are widespread, with high waves adding another threat to exposed coastal areas and islands.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japanese islands brace for Dujuan to become a typhoon again

articles.author: Louisa Loveluck
articles.description:
After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries. An in-depth investigation reveals the ‘show of force’ costing American taxpayers millions
No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Two leaders meet in French territory off Canada as Ottawa seeks stronger relations with EU while fighting trade war with US
The leaders of France and Canada have pledged closer ties to grapple with rising geopolitical tensions, climate change and the erosion of democratic values, after ⁠they met in a ⁠French territory off Canada’s Atlantic coast.
The two leaders’ visit to Saint-Pierre ​and Miquelon – the first by a French president since 2014 and the first by a Canadian prime minister – came just weeks ⁠after Donald Trump posted an image showing the islands, as well as all of Canada and other countries in North America, covered by the US flag.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron and Carney announce closer France-Canada ties amid Trump tensions

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Jovenel Moïse, 53, was shot dead in July 2021 in a killing which sparked chaos in Haiti
Eighteen people have been arrested in association with the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, according to US officials.
Moïse, 53, was shot dead on 7 July 2021 at his private residence by a hired group of about 20 military-trained Colombian mercenaries. His security detail did not intervene to protect him.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than a dozen arrested in connection with 2021 assassination of Haitian president

articles.author: Patrick Wintour in New York
articles.description:
Tensions grow as Trump tells Fox News he is considering ‘wiping Iran out’ after attacks on Riyadh by Houthi rebels
Governments across the Middle East are bracing for an escalation of violence after Iran claimed it had received intelligence that the US was preparing for a renewed bombing campaign against the Islamic Republic.
In a potential sign of growing tensions before the UN general assembly in New York this week, Donald Trump cut short a weekend visit to the Camp David presidential retreat on Sunday with no official explanation, and a new security alert was issued by the state department to all US citizens in the Middle East.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East braces for more violence as Iran claims US is planning to renew bombing campaign

articles.author: Rebecca Bailey China correspondent
articles.description:
Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and pace

China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenario

About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.
His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development

articles.author: Donna Ferguson, Yassin El-Moudden and agencies
articles.description:
Authorities issued warnings for city in first such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July
Yemen’s Houthis said they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport on Saturday.
The Saudi government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks, marking the first time the government has issued such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport as Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital

articles.author: Maanvi Singh
articles.description:
Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence

Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.
The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan and agencies
articles.description:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children
Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.
The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences
Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.
Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Four of Nusrat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week
A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed.
Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout

articles.author: Agence France-Presse and Associated Press
articles.description:
Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing  Tunchanok Donhomla 
An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said.
Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty

articles.author: James Michelin for MetDesk
articles.description:
At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia 
Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person.
Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon

articles.author: Mark Sweney and agencies
articles.description:
Increase from 1% to 1.25% follows US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank tightening monetary policy

Business live – latest updates

Japan’s central bank has increased interest rates to a fresh 31-year high as it attempts to combat global inflation linked to the war in Iran.
The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to raise its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high to curb impact of rising prices

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing 
An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.
A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IS member sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing

articles.author: Damien Gayle
articles.description:
Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August
Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found.
Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse, which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi and Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
articles.description:
Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim Munir
The sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.
Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Trump’s announcement on Russia ally comes as he steps up his trade war with Canada, a long-term US ally and top supplier of potash
President Donald Trump has said he is working on a “massive” deal to buy fertiliser from Belarus, pivoting away from main supplier Canada amid an escalating trade dispute, and moving instead toward an ally of Russia.
“The United States is working on a massive deal with respect to the purchase of Potash from Belarus,” Trump said on his Truth Social network. “The pricing would be for substantially less than we are currently paying to Canada, very good news for our farmers and ranchers.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump seeks ‘massive’ Belarus fertiliser deal amid Canada trade war

articles.author: Coral Murphy Marcos, Chris Hippensteel, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

The three news outlets President Trump banned from the White House last Friday have filed their anticipated lawsuit against his administration to restore their access.
In the new complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on Monday, CNN, MS Now and Politico alleged that Trump had violated the First Amendment and due process by stripping the outlets of their White House access in a blatant act of retaliation for coverage he disliked.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says he’ll probably lose lawsuit brought by news outlets he banned from White House, blaming judge appointed by ‘TRUMP’ – as it happened

articles.author: Ariana Baio in New York and Maanvi Singh
articles.description:
White House promoted its own ‘Trump TV’ feed online after ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC decline to participate
The major US television news outlets agreed to suspend their video coverage of Donald Trump after the administration banned journalists from several outlets from entering the White House grounds.
The collective decision came after the barred outlets – CNN, MS Now and Politico – sued the administration on Monday, saying the president’s actions were a violation of their first amendment rights.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

articles.author: José Olivares in New York and David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Republican president said he hoped the democratic socialist would be a ‘great mayor’ for New York City
Donald Trump said on Monday that he hoped Zohran Mamdani would be a “great mayor” for New York, an unusually warm assessment of the democratic socialist leader whom the president and his Republican allies have spent months holding up as a symbol of the Democratic party’s alleged embrace of “communism” ahead of the November midterms.
At a news conference following their closed-door meeting at Gracie Mansion, Trump and Mamdani appeared friendly as they have in previous meetings. Mamdani said he and Trump held a “wide-ranging” discussion, which touched on affordable housing and immigration, but did not offer extensive details regarding any disagreements between them.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump and Mamdani appear friendly after ‘wide-ranging’ meeting at Gracie Mansion

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Thousands of flights were delayed or canceled after a primary line failed and a backup fiber-optic cable was severed
Airport operations across the US north-east resumed Monday evening after a communications line failure snarled flights at some of the country’s busiest airports, leading to thousands of flight cancellations and delays.
Flights were halted at several airports after a primary communications line failed at a key Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) facility in Philadelphia. The backup fiber optic line, which delivers internet service, was inadvertently severed by a railroad construction crew, resulting in a telecommunications crash and hundreds of canceled flights at Newark, LaGuardia, JFK, Philadelphia and Boston airports.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flights resume across US north-east after FAA communications failure

articles.description:
Protesters in Austin, Texas, demonstrated against the Trump administration’s hardline anti-immigration campaign after an ICE agent shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon. Eyewitness footage filmed moments after the shooting shows the ICE officer standing next to an open car door, in which there is a visible dent. The man, identified by relatives and his lawyer as 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, was taken to a hospital in Austin in a serious but stable condition, officials said, before being taken into custody.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, said it was leading an investigation into the officer involved in the shooting, with the help of the FBI. Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, mayor Kirk Watson stated at a press conference 

ICE agent shoots and wounds Venezuelan man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters gather in Austin after ICE agent shoots and wounds man – video

articles.author: Margaret Sullivan
articles.description:
CNN, MS Now and Politico accurately call last week’s sudden lockout ‘a direct assault on the first amendment’. That’s right
On Monday, the three news organizations that had been kicked out of the White House because of Donald Trump’s latest fit of pique sued the president and three top advisers.
An accompanying statement by CNN, MS Now and Politico accurately calls last week’s sudden lockout “a direct assault on the first amendment”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Washington press corps needs to boycott White House events   | Margaret Sullivan

articles.author: Alice Speri
articles.description:
Media workers are grappling with increasingly volatile press climate in US, with some detained and even deported

Banished: Trump’s secret deportation deals

What is Trump’s third-country deportation policy?

As hundreds of masked and armed US federal agents besieged the streets of Minneapolis, turning the midwestern city into the frontline of the Trump administration’s unprecedented crackdown on immigration, the independent photographer John Abernathy was documenting one of the protests that had become a daily occurrence when Immigration and Customs Enforcement tackled him.
A photograph of him on the ground, pepper spray running down his face, captured the violence with which ICE agents had for weeks treated immigrants and the thousands of US citizens who had come to their defence. It was also a stark reminder that journalists were not immune to the agency’s aggressive tactics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Freedom oppressed: the journalists caught up in Trump’s ICE crackdown

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
While world leaders prepare for annual UN gathering, shifts in the global order continue in the face of a disruptive American president
In the event of a midterms election battering, it is possible that a deflated Donald Trump, constrained by a Democrat-controlled Congress, will gradually have to face up to the indignity of irrelevance.
While continuing to sign off Truth Social posts with his usual, “Thank you for your attention to this matter”, no one will actually be paying much attention. His meandering press conferences will no longer be carried live by TV networks. The Republican party will move on to the question of his successor. Trump could announce he had changed the name of the Champs-Élysées to Sunset Boulevard and even Google Maps will stifle a yawn. He would become that most pitied of political animals, the lame duck.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Whiplashed middle powers seek new alliances as Trump rages on world stage

articles.author: Michael Sainato
articles.description:
Trump says he digs coal – but pneumoconiosis cases are at a 50-year high, and sick miners are mired in benefit delays
For 38 years, Josh Armes worked as a coal miner in West Virginia and Virginia.
After retirement, Armes, 74, of Grundy, Virginia, was diagnosed with black lung disease, medically known as coal workers’ pneumoconiosis (CWP), caused by breathing in coal dust over long periods, which irreversibly damages the lungs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Do you have to be dead?’: US coalminers plead for benefits as black-lung disease cases surge

articles.author: Robert Tait in Braddock, Pennsylvania
articles.description:
The maverick senator has isolated himself from supporters as he has become a strident supporter of Israel
Two eras, two videos, shot against the same physical backdrop, convey political messages that seem a world removed from each other.
The contrasting films, produced eight years apart, neatly distill the evolution of John Fetterman, Pennsylvania’s maverick senator in his journey from progressive icon to a man seemingly more at ease with his nominal Republican opponents than his fellow Democrats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I don’t trust him any more’: Pennsylvanians come to grips with John Fetterman’s rightwing turn

articles.author: Jared Abbott and Joan C Williams
articles.description:
The party needs to thread the needle between college-educated and working-class voters. Our survey offers a way
Resisting authoritarianism is the second-highest priority for Democrats’ college-educated base. But for working-class Americans, it’s only the 19th priority (out of 20), we found in a new survey. The gap between these two groups was larger than on any other issues: elites prioritized resisting authoritarianism an astonishing 33 percentage points more than non-elites did.
Democrats’ dilemma is that their college-educated base insists they stand up to Donald Trump’s attacks on democracy, but they also need to win working-class votes. The way to thread that needle is to recognize that what’s needed to defend democracy in the short term is different from what’s needed to defend it in the long term.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: To protect democracy, Democrats should talk about corruption – not authoritarianism | Jared Abbott and Joan C Williams

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland with Blake Montgomery , produced by Nada Smiljanic and John Rogers; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Tech bosses have called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence and formal guardrails to be introduced by the US government. But President Trump is not moved by the doomsday predictions, calling them a ‘hoax'. What is behind his affection for the AI industry? Jonathan Freedland and Guardian US tech editor Blake Montgomery discuss
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Trump’s AI obsession walking the world into disaster? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Martin J Riedl and Samuel Woolley
articles.description:
Secret coordination between politicians and social media creators is a form of astroturfing. But there are few legal regulations
Not long ago, it was common wisdom among social media influencers that they shouldn’t talk politics. There was a widespread belief among their crowd that it was bad for business. If you went left, you lost the right, and vice-versa.
Times have changed. Nearly everywhere you look online, influencers are posting political content. Each day, there are new reports detailing their hot takes on elections, campaigns and the culture wars. It’s become a lucrative business for these creators, as they now like to be called, and a boost for those that pay them for hype.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Paid influencers are everywhere in US politics. We need transparency | Martin J Riedl and Samuel Woolley

articles.author: Vince Beiser
articles.description:
Trump himself has acknowledged the US need for Canadian aluminum – and has largely exempted metals from new tariffs
As trade talks with Canada shambled toward collapse in late August, Donald Trump brayed on Truth Social: “WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!” But in fact, Canada, like China, has something the US needs badly: critical metals that undergird modern military technology.
Canada is the United States’s biggest foreign source of minerals, supplying about $47bin worth each year. Sixty per cent of all the aluminum the US uses each year, for instance, comes from Canada, where mighty, remote rivers provide smelting plants vast quantities of cheap, low-carbon electricity. The US military uses the lightweight metal for everything from shell casings to ship hulls and aircraft fuselage. The Pentagon’s cutting-edge F-35 fighter jet’s airframe is about 40% aluminum. “This country desperately needs aluminum,” Trump complained last month. “We get it all from Canada for the most part, and we need it badly.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says the US doesn’t need Canada. But it’s the source of key minerals for the military | Vince Beiser

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Johana Bhuiyan . Produced by Tiara Chiaramonte engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producers Jonathan Menjivar and Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
A former Anthropic researcher’s apocalyptic declaration about artificial intelligence has led to a global panic that the technology might be the end of us all. At an event in Washington today to warn about the dangers of AI, US senator Bernie Sanders said that Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel'. Oddly, Steve Bannon appeared at the same event. But is this response a distraction from the more immediate problems AI is already causing? Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian tech reporter Johana Bhuyian to put this moment in context, and she explains why we should be cynical about industry calls for regulation
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the real AI apocalypse is already here – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.description:
During a Senate committee hearing, FBI director answered questions from Republican senator John Kennedy about the bureau's new policy allowing the hiring of people who have engaged in bestiality
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kash Patel defends changes in FBI hiring policy regarding bestiality – video

articles.author: Amelia Hill
articles.description:
Women escaping abusive partners abroad could get new protections from legal analysis of Hague convention
British mothers who bring their children with them when returning to the UK after fleeing from domestic abuse abroad – which can lead to them being accused of abduction – could be given greater legal protection and support.
The government has agreed to examine how domestic abuse features in international child abduction cases, with a view to giving survivors of domestic abuse more help fighting partners’ demands that they return children to their home countries.
In the UK, call the national domestic abuse helpline on 0808 2000 247, or visit Women’s Aid. In the US, the domestic violence hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). In Australia, the national family violence counselling service is on 1800 737 732. Other international helplines may be found via www.befrienders.org.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hope for UK mothers accused of child abduction after fleeing domestic violence

articles.author: Helena Smith in Nicosia
articles.description:
Human rights lawyer says accused father is victim of ‘archaic system’ after boy fell from window in July
A British father is expected to appear in court in Cyprus accused of “recklessly” causing the death of his two-year-old son, who was fatally injured falling from a fourth-floor window.
The 37-year-old, who has not been named publicly, was on the first day of a family holiday in Paphos on 12 July when the toddler died.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Briton due to face Cypriot court after tragic death of two-year-old son

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Will Parman
articles.description:
Experts say trend across England probably reflects swifter access to diagnoses as wealthier families go private
Some of the most affluent areas of England have had the sharpest rises in the proportion of young people claiming disability benefits for ADHD and autism since the pandemic, according to new research.
Claims for the personal independence payment (Pip) benefit for these health conditions were typically proportionally far higher in deprived areas with higher rates of poverty, low educational outcomes and insecure employment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Young people’s Pip claims for ADHD and autism ‘rising fastest in affluent areas’

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
System gives patients, loved ones and health workers the right to ask for a second opinion on care
Martha’s rule, which lets NHS patients, staff and relatives request a review of their care, is being expanded to every A&E in England, health officials have announced.
The system gives patients, their loved ones and health workers the right to ask for a different medical team to examine the care being provided on inpatient wards and to recommend changes. It has already potentially saved hundreds of lives, official figures show.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Martha’s rule to be expanded to every A&E in England

articles.author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
articles.description:
Changes could save £33bn and result in average of four extra years of good health for people, report says
The NHS in England could prevent 20,000 deaths and save £33bn a year by cutting red tape and boosting productivity, a report says.
Research by the Health Foundation found the health service has been held back for decades by excessive regulation, short-term planning and insufficient capability to deliver major change.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cut NHS red tape and boost productivity to prevent 20,000 early deaths a year in England, report urges

articles.author: Alexandra Topping and Peter Walker
articles.description:
At Lib Dems’ conference in Brighton, leader will accuse Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and ‘tech bros’ to solve problem
Ed Davey is to call for a global nuclear-style non-proliferation treaty to halt the development of super-intelligent AI when he makes his keynote speech at the Liberal Democrat conference, accusing Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and “tech bros” to solve the problem.
When he addresses the faithful on the final day of the gathering in Brighton, the party leader will call for a global pause on super-intelligent AI, comparing it to a nuclear arms race that could result in technology that could “destroy us all”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Halt super-intelligent AI with non-proliferation treaty, Ed Davey to say

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Nats says fault at Prestwick has been ‘fixed’ after airports in Scotland, northern England and Northern Ireland are hit
Airlines have called for “action and accountability” over the UK’s air traffic control services after a technical issue led to flights being disrupted for the second time in a fortnight.
Dozens were cancelled and others severely delayed after a fault on Monday morning at National Air Traffic Services (Nats), this time at its second control centre at Prestwick in South Ayrshire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Airlines urge action after UK flights delayed and cancelled again

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Motion passed at party conference calls for new approach to implementing ruling that legal definition of a woman is based on biological sex only
The Liberal Democrats have rejected official guidance by the equalities watchdog on how organisations should implement the supreme court ruling on transgender people, calling it “discriminatory and unworkable”.
The motion, passed overwhelmingly at the party’s annual conference in Brighton, makes the Lib Dems the first of the big three parties in parliament to call for a new approach to implementing last year’s ruling that the legal definition of a woman is based on biological sex only. The Greens have previously done so.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lib Dems reject ‘discriminatory and unworkable’ EHRC guidance on transgender people

articles.author: Steven Morris and Geneva Abdul
articles.description:
Lawyer tells hearing that families wish to know whether weaponry involved in deaths was made in Britain
Israeli and UK military commanders could be requested to give evidence to an inquest concerning three British workers killed in Gaza when aid vehicles they were travelling in were hit by an airstrike.
It is also possible that the inquest into the deaths of John Chapman, 57, Jim Henderson, 33, and James Kirby, 47, may examine whether the weaponry that killed the men was made in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Inquest into British aid workers killed in Gaza may call on Israeli and UK military chiefs

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Nigel Farage dismisses loss of previous leader as ‘bump in the road’ and says party will ‘carry on as if nothing has happened’

Nigel Farage dismissed the loss of Reform UK’s leader in Wales last week as a “bump in the road” as the party unveiled a replacement.
Helen Jenner replaces Dan Thomas, who stood down last Tuesday after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviours.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Helen Jenner unveiled as Reform UK’s new leader in Wales after arrest of Dan Thomas

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
The number of potentially damaging environmental incidents triggered by this year’s hot and dry weather has surpassed that of 2025
Wildlife in England and Wales will be affected by the current drought for years to come, the government has said.
This summer saw large parts of England and all of Wales plunged into a serious drought, with both recording their driest Julys since records began in 1836.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Wildlife will be affected by current drought for years to come, UK government says

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Small traders and drivers bear the brunt of a refining shortage taking forecourt prices towards £2 a litre as wars wipe out about a fifth of global supplies
The smoke rising from the Kapotnya oil refinery to the south-east of Moscow marks one of Ukraine’s biggest air raids on the Russian capital since the start of the war, and the latest salvo in an energy crisis that threatens to affect households and businesses across the globe.
More than 1,500 miles away, British motorists are braced for the ripple effect from that conflict, and the US-Israel war on Iran. Average UK diesel prices are expected to reach record highs within days – while across Europe and the US, pump prices have already surpassed all-time highs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Half my day’s pay goes to filling up my car now’: diesel crisis ripples across Britain

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
Helen Jenner will be party’s new head in Senedd after a narrow victory over Jason O’Connell
Here are some more lines from Max Wilkinson’s speech to the Lib Dem conference this morning.
Wilkinson, the Lib Dem home affairs spokesperson, accused Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, of using “divisive language” that you would expect from the “authoritarian right”. After condemning the Tories and Reform UK for their anti-migration views, he said:
And what’s the Labour response to this hard right agenda? Their home secretary has indulged in the sort of divisive language that we would usually expect from the authoritarian right …
Well let me tell you home secretary – no matter how hard you chase, you’ll never catch up with [Nigel] Farage – that is a fool’s errand.
He said that it was the duty of the Liberal Democrats to stand up to the Tories and Reform UK, and the “poison” they were spreading on migration. Repeatedly referring to Reform UK’s Robert Jenrick as a “plonker”, he said:
[Jenrick] and his party are plonkers with dangerous ideas … and £72m to deliver them.
And their allies in the Conservative party are weakly following them.
He criticised the Conservatives and Reform UK for proposing to withdraw Britain from the European convention on human rights. He said:
Leaving the European convention on human rights will not fix our asylum system.
It will not stop dangerous Channel crossings – not a single boat – and it will not stop the criminal gangs.
And he confirmed that the Lib Dems want to tax big tech to finance a new online crime agency. This was announced overnight and Peter Walker and Alexandra Topping have written the story up here.
We will carry on as if nothing has happened

 We could have done without this bump in the road. But it has happened, We are making the best of it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics: New leader of Reform UK in Wales named after defeating rival by just two votes – as it happened

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by John Rogers and Nada Smiljanic, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
The UK prime minister will meet the US president for the first time in New York on Tuesday. With Trump at his weakest in the polls, could this be a perfect moment for Burnham to charm the president and avoid a very public political spat? Pippa and Kiran discuss what the two leaders might discuss in policy terms, and some of the potential high-risk issues
Please keep sending your comments and questions to Pippa and Kiran on politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com
Watch this episode and subscribe to our YouTube channel here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Andy Burnham pull off the ‘Mamdani effect’ on Donald Trump? – podcast

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Residents say new legislation in England forcing landlords to fix dangerous hazards is not improving conditions
Sarah Killick has been battling problems in her social home for months, including mould and damp. She says the anxiety has been insufferable and she has permanently damaged her teeth from grinding them due to stress.
She thought help would come in the form of Awaab’s law, new legislation designed to force social housing landlords in England to fix dangerous hazards, which came into effect in October last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Awaab’s law is not working, say social housing tenants stuck in mouldy homes

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Blow to John Healey before budget as UK households face ‘notable strain’ on their finances
Fears of a steep rise in mortgage payments and increasing job insecurity have sent UK consumer confidence tumbling to a three-month low, according to a leading survey.
In a blow to John Healey before next month’s budget, the S&P Global consumer sentiment index dropped to 42.7 in September from 42.9 in August, indicating “a notable strain on financial confidence across UK households”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fears over interest rate rise and jobs send UK consumer confidence to three-year low

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Claimants having to find decades-old medical records to prove they qualify for compensation despite inquiry’s recommendations
Suzanne Morgan will never forget the day her mother died. It was nine months after she had gone into hospital with gallstones, where she received a routine blood transfusion.
“She went downhill rapidly,” Morgan recalled. Her mother haemorrhaged in her liver, and the next day she was dead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I have to keep reliving it’: infected blood claimants being asked to prove eligibility

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Eco-moorings help to restore seagrass in just five years, boosting sealife such as seahorses, eels and crabs
One of the UK’s most precious underwater habitats – Dorset’s seagrass meadows – is recovering thanks to “eco moorings” designed to prevent the seabed being ripped up, a study has revealed.
Scars caused by traditional anchors in some areas of seagrass in Studland Bay have almost entirely vanished, which is boosting the number of seahorses that thrive in the submerged meadows.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Incredibly encouraging’: healing the scars of traditional anchors in Dorset’s seagrass meadows

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests
Google has been fined more than €400m (£345m) over the way it processed users’ location data, following claims that the tech giant had manipulated users into agreeing to be constantly tracked on their mobile phones.
The fine, imposed by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC), comes after complaints from multiple European consumer organisations that Google was following every step users took.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Google fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location data

articles.author: Mark Sweney and Robert Booth
articles.description:
Jensen Huang dismisses warnings from former Anthropic researcher and others as ‘doomsday narratives’ 
The boss of the chipmaker Nvidia has said AI will not develop to a point that will lead to the extinction of the human race within a few years, rejecting such assertions as overblown “doomsday narratives”.
Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of the $5tn AI chipmaker, said the claims made on social media by the former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that AI could become “superhuman” and kill off humanity within the decade were “irresponsible”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia boss says there is ‘0% chance’ AI destroys the world by 2030

articles.author: Matthew Ponsford
articles.description:
Exclusive: The tax-funded brainchild of Dominic Cummings hopes to find ways to speed up wild species’ evolution
Vaccines for ash trees, skin treatments for newts and gene-edited swallowtail butterflies are among 14 tax-funded projects from the UK’s “invention agency” aiming to accelerate nature’s ability to adapt to the climate crisis.
The £54m accelerated adaptation programme from the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria) – a public body that funds high-risk, high-reward tech projects – aims to investigate applications of biotechnology that can speed up wild species’ evolution and help them to adapt to new threats such as global warming and disease.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tree vaccines and gene-edited butterflies among biotechnology projects funded by UK ‘invention agency’

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff in Jersey
articles.description:
While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing
On a late Friday afternoon on the Channel Island of Jersey, tourists and locals are flocking to St Helier’s waterfront where the town’s sprawling beach has emerged at low tide.
In one direction, they face the calm waters of St Aubin’s Bay, ringed by a seaside promenade and punctuated with a tidal island hosting the 16th century Elizabeth Castle.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s unrecognisable’: How being a tax haven has changed Jersey

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Peter Walker; produced by Saskia Collette and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
From hospital wards to bathrooms, where is a transgender person supposed to go after the latest equalities guidance?
Transgender people in Britain are navigating a new reality. In August, new guidance – in the form of a document nearly 350 pages long – was published to help institutions interpret last year’s supreme court ruling on trans rights.
It means, as Amelia outlines to Helen Pidd, that every time she goes to a pub or restaurant, she is terrified about going to the bathroom. As a trans woman, she has used women’s facilities without problems for years; now she’s being told she should use the men’s.
 Continue reading...

For those who hadn’t yet seen one, the magazine described it as “not that much different in principle from an ordinary brush – you have a stick with a brush on the end. The difference is that an electric one moves the brush head for you”. Progress indeed.
Nearly six decades on, electric toothbrushes can do a lot more than merely jiggle, offering multiple speeds and movement sensors for real-time tracking of where you’ve brushed – some even promise gum-massage or tongue-cleaning modes. Prices range from about £25 for a basic Oral B model to £599.99 for a Philips Sonicare model that gives “smart coverage feedback”. The latest super-toothbrush – a mere £419.99 – features a camera and a built-in water jet to clean between teeth, using AI to identify gaps. Created by Dyson, it’s still, essentially, a stick with a brush on the end (although there is another toothbrush on the market that’s shaped like a mouthguard, with individual brushes, that claims to clean your teeth in 20 seconds).

You spend a considerable portion of Silent Hill: Townfall in a kind of foetal position, cowering behind objects that will be eerily familiar to anyone who lived in the UK during the 1990s. Cars seem to be modelled on the era’s boxy Volkswagen Golfs; logos adorning phone boxes should narrowly escape the attention of copyright lawyers at BT Group. (For millennials, the deja vu will likely intensify the horror, as if stepping back into a childhood nightmare.) Simon, the nerdy, unassuming star of the game, pokes his head around corners to catch a glimpse of the demonic entities that wish to maim him, before shrinking back down again with a downwards motion of the analogue stick. In such moments, it’s easy to imagine him wrapping his arms around his knees, clasping his eyes shut and wishing himself away from this place.
The game’s setting, St Amelia, is based on the fishing communities of the East Neuk of Fife. The terror lurking here is wonderfully specific: absent lairds, island poverty, an oil-drilling corporation. Anguished beasts lumber down quaint streets lined with sandstone houses and fluttering bunting. This venerable horror series may have shifted to Scotland, yet we remain firmly in classic Silent Hill territory – weather and all. St Amelia finds itself suffused in supernatural fog and the vast majority of its inhabitants have vanished following some kind of mass tragedy. The artful, evocative presentation is such that you can almost taste the in-game air, the briny seaside tang diluted by rainy mist.

articles.description:
After a week of alarming warnings about artificial intelligence’s potential to destroy the world as we know it, our technology reporters answered your questions on the reality of the AI threat 

IcommentthereforeIam asks: Given our senses, emotions, memory and moods, is it ever going to be accepted that humanly conscious AI is fantasy?
Dan: This is a serious question that has even rattled Richard Dawkins, the evolutionary biologist. He may not believe that God is real but he does believe that AI is conscious - or at least the chatbot he was using, which he called Claudia. “You may not know you are conscious, but you bloody well are,” he wrote.
And he’s not the first. In 2022 Google fired an engineer who went public with his belief that a company-developed AI had feelings. At the more troubling end of this belief, there are countless examples of people becoming overly attached to, and influenced by, AI chatbots – including cases of psychosis.
Aisha: There’s certainly a theatrical – even “psy-op”- quality to the flurry of AI doomsaying over the past weeks. It’s hard to say entirely what concrete developments are at the root of it all. We know that the Hugging Face incident, where a “swarm” of AI agents hacked another company, has been one trigger of the drama. There have been other contributing incidents too – Dario Amodei suggests internal developments at Anthropic have prompted his latest round of blogging, and there’s been some X discourse and doomy muttering about bioweapons.
We aren’t in the heads of Dario Amodei or Sam Altman, and so we cannot say how sincere they are, and how much they might have other goals in mind – such as, perhaps, delaying their IPOs until their finances look better. But any company of their size, and with their potential liabilities, would be angling hard to be regulated as favourably as possible. That’s what big companies do.

articles.author: Keza MacDonald
articles.description:
The first console I ever bought, it was hyped as a threat to the PlayStation, then mocked as a flop. But now, as it marks its 25th anniversary, it’s looked back on with misty-eyed reverence 
This week marks the 25th anniversary of the Nintendo GameCube, the first console I ever bought with my own money. I vividly remember getting on the bus after school with a year’s worth of savings safely zipped into the pocket of my bag and going to a branch of Currys, where I dumped a bunch of notes, coins and vouchers on the counter to collect my pre-order. (It turned out that some of the vouchers from the previous Christmas had expired, but the guy at the checkout clearly felt so sorry for me that he redeemed them anyway. If you’re out there, Currys guy: thank you for taking pity on a desperate 13-year-old.)
If it hadn’t been for the ill-fated Wii U console, whose failure to take off in 2012 resulted in the first unprofitable periods in Nintendo’s game-making history, the GameCube would be remembered as the company’s biggest flop aside from the infamous Virtual Boy, from 1995. Released in Japan this week in 2001 (and in May 2002 in Europe), this surprisingly powerful purple cube sold much less than the Xbox and the PlayStation 2. With its squat, colourful form and unusual controller, arranged around a big traffic-light-green A button and small analogue sticks designed for small hands, it had a hint of Fisher-Price about it.

The distinctively British RPG is returning courtesy of the makers of Forza Horizon – with comedy talent such as Richard Ayoade and Natasia Demetriou voicing sweary characters. We had our first play and spoke to its developer

When Playground Games was founded in 2010, its objective was straightforward: to make the best cars in video games. Operating out of an unassuming white building in Leamington Spa, the studio sought to challenge Gran Turismo with its critically acclaimed British racing alternative: the acclaimed free-roaming Forza Horizon series. Yet as the team grew, so did their ambitions. Now they are making the most intriguing British fantasy game we have seen in many years.
For those who have never ventured into Albion, Fable is a quintessentially British role playing game. Created by Lionhead Studios for the original Xbox in 2004, it boasted cheeky charm alongside world-altering player choices, and its droll writing was brought to life in later iterations by national treasures such as Stephen Fry and Simon Pegg. Thanks to its unique blend of farce and fantasy, Fable grew into a globally beloved franchise – before Microsoft unceremoniously shuttered Lionhead in 2016, after mandating that the studio turn its star series into a multiplayer game. The result, Fable Legends, was never released.

We have a first play of the forthcoming Tomb Raider remake and speak with its developers. Can they improve on the gameplay without losing what made the 1996 original such a classic?
We join Lara Croft in St Francis’ Folly – inspired by the Unesco-listed monasteries of Meteora in Greece – as the light shines through the cracked ceiling and a flock of bats glide across the vast ruins below. When Lara leaps down to the monastery’s crumbling pillared courtyard, it becomes clear that these screeching, leathery creatures aren’t just set dressing. As they lurch towards her with unpredictable movements, she dispatches the swarm with a flurry of gun fire and panicked punches.
It’s a suitably cinematic reintroduction to our heroine and her very first adventure. Co-developed by longtime Lara custodians Crystal Dynamics and Polish studio Flying Wild Hog, Legacy of Atlantis is a reimagining of the classic 1996 game Tomb Raider, and this familiar cliffside location is now brimming with new life and believable detail. Yet while our reunion gets off to an auspicious start, I have my concerns. It feels like reconnecting with an old friend at the pub, only for them to begin spouting conspiracy theories two pints in.
